summary: The Wind turbine profit calculator turns the price of electricity, the wind turbine profit and more into wind turbine cost. That makes it useful for a footprint, a resource or an environmental change you want to size up. The unit chips sit next to the boxes, which is where most hand-calculation mistakes start.

sections.title: How does the Wind turbine profit calculator work?
sections.html:
The Wind turbine profit calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports wind turbine cost in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case; then you type in the price of electricity, the wind turbine profit, the air flow area and the air density.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Wind turbine profit calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Wind turbine cost=price of electricity × wind turbine generated power − wind turbine profit
Time of generation=2 × total ENERGY! (not power) of the wind (TO BE HIDDEN) ÷ (air density × air flow area × (wind speed in your area ^ 3))
KW of the turbine (TO BE HIDDEN)=turbine efficiency × total ENERGY! (not power) of the wind (TO BE HIDDEN)
Time of generation=86400 × time in days (TO BE HIDDEN)
KW of the turbine (TO BE HIDDEN)=wind turbine generated power × time in days (TO BE HIDDEN)
Wind turbine generated power=(1 ÷ 3600000) × wind turbine generated power

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Energy, opening in kilowatt hours
  • Currency, opening in US Dollar
  • Currency, opening in US Dollar
  • Currency, opening in US Dollar
  • Area, opening in square meters
  • Density, opening in kilograms per cubic meter
  • Speed, opening in meters per second
  • %, opening in percent

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Wind turbine profit calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Comparing two options on the same basis
  • Putting a headline figure into context
  • Sizing an environmental impact in familiar units
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the price of electricity, the wind turbine profit and the air flow area — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Wind turbine profit calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns wind turbine cost, derived from the price of electricity, the wind turbine profit and the air flow area. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Wind turbine profit calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the price of electricity, the wind turbine profit, the air flow area and the air density, which is 8 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter wind turbine generated power (Wind turbine profit) in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Wind turbine generated power (Wind turbine profit) opens in kilowatt hours and the chip beside it offers 33 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There is one choice to make (1 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the Wind turbine profit calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
